https://www.theguardian.com/environment/.text: Pedro Sánchez: ‘It’s not enough to address the consequences of the climate emergency … we have to reduce its causes.’ Photograph: Mariscal/EPA View image in fullscreen Pedro Sánchez: ‘It’s not enough to address the consequences of the climate emergency … we have to reduce its causes.’ Photograph: Mariscal/EPA Climate crisis ‘Climate change kills’: Pedro Sánchez speaks plain truth to Spain’s deniers PM has long history of speaking out on realities of global heating but political opponents remain unnmoved Sam Jones in Madrid Sun 2 Aug 2026 00.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google J ust over four years ago, Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez , visited a small town in the south-western region of Extremadura that had been affected by one of the wildfires devouring tens of thousands of hectares of land across the country. That summer’s blazes had left two people dead in the northern region of Castilla y León and another man there fatally burned after the excavator he was using to try to dig a firebreak to protect his town was swallowed up by the flames. A street-sweeper in Madrid had collapsed and died from heatstroke while on shift in soaring temperatures that summer. The paramedics who tried to save him noted that his body temperature was 41.6C (107F). “I want to make something very clear,” the prime minister told reporters in Extremadura that day in 2022. “Climate change kills: it kills people, as we’ve seen; it also kills our ecosystem, our biodiversity, and it also destroys the things we as a society hold dear – our houses, our businesses, our livestock.” View image in fullscreen Pedro Sánchez (centre) visits fire-affected areas of Extremadura in 2022. Photograph: Ballesteros/EPA Earlier this week – amid wildfires that have consumed more than 180,000 hectares (428,915 acres) of land in the first seven months of 2026 – he repeated the same blunt warning. “The climate emergency kills,” he said on Monday . “And that’s why it’s not enough to address the consequences, which we do; what we have to do is reduce its causes, anticipate its effects, and, consequently, better prepare our country to protect people’s lives.” Just as he has been one of the most vociferous European leaders when it comes to criticising Israel’s conduct in Gaza and Donald Trump’s war in Iran - and defending the benefits of immigration – so Sánchez has long deployed unvarnished language to raise awareness of the climate emergency. On the face of it, that may come as little surprise: as a country on the southern frontier of the world’s fastest-heating continent, Spain is becoming increasingly vulnerable to the effects of the climate emergency, be they droughts, desertification, erratic weather patterns, heavy rains or wildfires. 11:13 Race against time to contain wildfires in France and Spain - The Latest Awareness, and perhaps personal experience, of the growing scale of the crisis is increasingly common. According to a survey published in December 2024 by Spain’s state research institute, the Centre for Research Studies, 84% of Spaniards see the climate emergency as “a real threat to human wellbeing and to the health of the planet”. Despite the floods and the fires, however, there is little political common ground, and opposition parties have rejected Sánchez’s plans for a “state pact” to prepare Spain for the climate emergency . On Monday, Spain’s conservative People’s party (PP) accused the government of using the “mantra” of climate crisis to mask its “poor management” of natural disasters. As well as claiming the Sánchez administration had seized on the climate emergency as a wedge issue, the PP’s spokesperson, Ester Muñoz, appeared to question the notion of a human-driven climate crisis. “That the climate changes is something that has occurred throughout the history of humanity and the Earth – that’s obvious,” she said. “Now how do we humans act in the face of things that change?” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Down to Earth The planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essential Preview latest after newsletter promotion View image in fullscreen A forest engineer surveys the wildfire damage in Ávila, Spain. Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters The PP’s record on the climate crisis and emergency response is, to put it mildly, mixed. When floods hit Valencia at the end of October 2024, its PP regional president – who eventually resigned – was having a three-hour lunch with a journalist and did not arrive at the response centre until the early evening, by which time many people had drowned in their homes, garages and cars. Europe burns: a visual guide to the wildfires Read more Unlike her erstwhile Valencian counterpart, the PP president of the Madrid region, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, has been quick to ask the central government to step in and assume overall control of the wildfire response. But Ayuso, a rightwing populist, has questioned the scientific basis of the climate emergency and claimed it is an “agenda” pushed by “lobbies” and “communists”. Her views are reminiscent of those held by the far-right Vox party, which is adamant that the current wildfires have nothing to do with the climate emergency and everything to do with a failure to clear rural areas of excess vegetation and to invest in firefighting services. The PP has forged a series of regional alliances with Vox, heralding a possible national coalition if it wins next year’s general election . Experts and climate scientists say the blazes are down to a combination of factors : the abandonment of rural areas; an abundance of highly flammable, dry vegetation, and an increase in heatwaves driven by climate breakdown. On Wednesday, a Vox MEP, Jorge Buxadé, attempted to push the party’s denial agenda by posting what purported to be an official air ministry document showing that temperatures of more than 44C had been recorded at observation stations around Spain as far back as the 1950s. Spain’s state meteorological office, Aemet, responded on social media by pointing out that the document was a fake. “We’ve reviewed the data, and all but one station’s data are false,” said Aemet . “If they were true, they wouldn’t deny climate change: there were heatwaves before, but now they’re more frequent and intense.” Explore more on these topics Climate crisis Spain Pedro Sánchez Europe Extreme heat Wildfires features Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

REUTERS/Issei Kato 31 July, 2026 Japan’s Seven & i Holdings has formed a strategic partnership with SoftBank Corp, PayPay and Sumitomo Mitsui Card, which will each invest 100 billion yen ($620 million) into the 7-Eleven operator, a filing showed on Friday. The total 300 billion yen investment comes after the 7-Eleven operator has struggled to turn around its business, having batted away a takeover attempt by Canadian convenience store rival Alimentation Couche-Tard last year. While Seven & i has carved out and sold off its less profitable business lines to focus on its core convenience stores, stiff competition in Japan and lacklustre results in North America have weighed on its profits. Each of Softbank, PayPay and Sumitomo Mitsui Card, the credit card arm of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, will acquire a 2.27% stake in Seven & i, the filing showed. Also on Friday, Seven & i announced a 400 billion yen share buyback, worth over 9% of its outstanding shares. Deal to bolster domestic business LY Corp, a SoftBank subsidiary that runs the Line messaging app along with a host of online businesses, also signed the strategic partnership, a release from the companies said. They aim to integrate their customer information and create a loyalty points ecosystem across Seven & i’s physical stores and the other companies’ online and financial customer bases, the filing said. The deal will bolster Seven & i’s higher-margin domestic business, but prospects for its larger international operations remain uncertain. Last week Seven & i aborted a potential stake purchase in Polish convenience store operator Zabka that would have expanded its presence in Europe beyond its strongholds in Japan and the U.S. It has failed to translate its $21 billion purchase of Speedway petrol stations in the U.S. into higher profitability, which has added to longstanding pressure from shareholders for higher returns. Since Couche-Tard pulled its 2,600 yen per share buyout offer in July last year, Seven & i’s shares have stagnated. They closed at 2,109 yen on Friday. A grant from the state Department of Transportation is expected to help alleviate backups and delays at traffic signals along state Route 309 in Wright Twp. Township officials this week were notified the municipality has been awarded a $159,144 Pennsylvania 2026 Green Light-Go grant for its traffic signal enhancement project. “We are excited that we are going to modernize the traffic lights and hope this solves the timing issues,” said Pamela Heard, township manager. She noted that the project will involve modernization of the timing technology for traffic signals at Crestwood Drive, William Sword Drive and Church Road. It also will include installation of small backup generators so that the traffic signal lights will stay on in the event of a power interruption. Rice Twp. news The Rice Twp. police department is sponsoring a back-to-school supply drive to help make sure local students have the tools they need for a successful school year. Through Aug. 20, the department is collecting new school supplies including pencils, crayons, notebooks, pocket folders, pencil cases, children’s scissors, glue sticks, rulers, erasers, pencil sharpeners and backpacks. Donations can be dropped off at the Rice Twp. municipal building, 3000 Church Road. Earlier this year, Rice Twp. applied for a $70,000 state grant earmarked for the Nuangola Drive project. With the state’s budget in place, township officials said they expect the funds to be released, allowing the project to move forward. The township has applied for a $1 million state Department of Community and Economic Development multimodal grant to resurface roads in Woodland Estates, Polonia Estates and Woodberry Manor. The work was recommended by PennDOT Local Technical Assistance Project consultant. The township also plans to investigate solutions for the flooding of Aleksander Boulevard and rework Weyhenmeyer Road drainage. Stone Henge paving project Wright Twp. supervisors at a special meeting last week awarded a $308,704 contract to HRI Inc. for the Stone Hedge paving project. The project will be funded through a $150,000 Local Share Account grant and Liquid Fuel money. Earlier this summer, the company was awarded a $849,290 contract for paving Walden Drive from Route 309 to an area near Red Coat Road. The work also includes the reconstruction of the entrance to Walden Park. Movie in the park Wright Twp. Family Night in the Park will be held Friday, August 14 at the township park with the movie “Minecraft” set to begin at dusk. The movie is free and open to the public. Bring a chair or blanket to sit on to watch the movie Lonestar Sno Cone truck will be on hand to sell snow cones. Mountain Top Hose Co. 1 news Mountain Top Hose Co. 1 recently received $4,500 from U.S. Rep. Rob Bresnahan, R-8, Dallas, and his wife, Chelsea Bresnahan’s Green Light Project, which is administered by The Luzerne Foundation. The money will be used for a new furnace for the apparatus bay to keep equipment in a climate-controlled environment, prolonging its lifespan and keeping it ready in all weather. The hose company auxiliary will hold a potato pancake pop-up on Friday, August 28. Cost is $2 each or three for $5. Pre-orders are required for orders of two dozen or more to keep the lines moving. https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-europe-us-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5O1Lb Witkoff and Kushner have been trying to broker a deal to end the war for months Image: Ukrainian Presidential Press Office/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Ukrainian and European officials are set to meet US President Donald Trump's envoys in Miami on Friday to discuss "new ideas" to end Russia's war in Ukraine . Ukraine 's President Volodomyr Zelenskyy confirmed the meeting on Thursday evening, after a Russian attack on buses killed 30 civilians in the frontline city of Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine. Before the strikes in Kramatorsk, a Russian missile hit a five-storey apartment block in the northern Chernihiv region, killing 22 Ukrainians, including five children. More than 70 people have been killed in Russian strikes on Ukraine in the past two days, Zelenskyy said. The capital Kyiv again came under attack this week Image: Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS What did Zelenskyy say about the Miami meeting? "The Ukrainian negotiating team is due to meet Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff in the US tomorrow," Zelenskyy said. "The meeting is expected to last two days. We are also counting on a European team to join our negotiating group." Zelenskyy's chief of staff, Kyrylo Budanov, and other top officials, including Rustem Umerov, Sergiy Kyslytsya and David Arakhamia, will also attend, the Ukrainian president said. "They will discuss new ideas and proposals that American negotiators began developing with the Russians and Ukrainians during their recent visit to the region ", one of the US sources familiar with the talks told AFP. "They are all nervous about the winter. It will be a tough winter if the war does not stop," the US source said. Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting civilians, which the Kremlin denies Image: State Emergency Service of Ukraine/Handout/Anadolu/picture alliance Zelenskyy blames US for inaction Amid rising civilian casualties and fears of further escalation, Zelenskyy urged the US to accede to his request to expand Ukraine's access to Elon Musk's Starlink satellite service, which would help it target Russian ballistic-missile launchers. "Open Starlink for Ukraine. You did open it when you were responding to Iran ... I've said quite openly — give it to us, help us defend our skies and dominate there. And then Putin will sit down at ‌the negotiating table," he said. Zelenskyy went on to accuse the US of being unwilling to pressure Russia into negotiations, adding that enabling Starlink would cost Washington nothing. "So where's the truth here, where's the honesty? Where's the stalemate? ... That's called unwillingness," he said. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Thursday that he agreed with Rubio's assessment, adding that he saw no immediate prospect for a three-way summit between Russian President Vladimir Putin, Zelenskyy and Trump. "One cannot, on the one hand, negotiate with the Russians about future economic projects, whilst on ​the other hand say that we find ourselves in some sort of ... diplomatic stalemate," Zelenskyy said, countering the US narrative. "We are not a diplomatic dead end," he said. Zelenskyy also called for tougher sanctions to cripple the Russian economy, a point Ukrainian officials are expected to press US envoys on at the meeting. https://hvg.hu/tudomany/20261111_japan-g.text: Komoly kibertámadás ért egy japán céget, összesen több mint 20 000 szerver fertőződhetett meg. Komoly pénzjutalom járhat annak, aki segít megtalálni az elkövetőket. 1 millió dollárt, azaz körülbelül 325 millió forintot ajánl a japán GMO Internet Group technológiai cég annak, aki segít elkapni a Onamae.com platformot feltörő támadókat – számolt be róla a The Hacker News . A jutalom csak akkor jár, ha a bejelentés letartóztatáshoz vagy nemzetközi körözési parancs kiadásához vezet. A támadást október 20-án észlelte a GMO, amely devizakereskedéshez igazított virtuális Windows-környezeteket működtet. A rosszindulatú felek az ügyfelek szervereire telepítettek kártevőket. A cég egy nappal később elkezdte leállítani az érintett szervereket – ezekből összesen 26 739-at fertőzhettek meg a támadók. A GMO közölte: ügyféladatok is kiszivárogtak, és olyan tranzakciók is történtek, amelyeket nem a felhasználók indítottak. A támadók követelése több mint 50 millió dollárnak, azaz körülbelül 16 milliárd forintnak megfelelő japán jen, amelyet nem szeretnének kifizetni. Több mint 200 000 ügyfele van a Beget nevű orosz IT-cégnek, amelynek most abszolút nulláról kell felépítenie mindent. A GMO Cybercrime Bounty nevű jutalomprogramhoz egy dedikált weboldalt is létrehozott a cég. Ezen minden elérhetőség megtalálható, amelyeken keresztül akár névtelen tippeket is lehet küldeni a jutalom reményében. Ha máskor is tudni szeretne hasonló dolgokról, lájkolja a HVG Tech rovatának Facebook-oldalát .
